criteria.criterion: verify.suggest_duplicate_tickets is the canonical boolean (default False) on VerifyConfig with its _SECTIONS["verify"] coercer, and verify.overlap_enabled is no longer a live key
An existing project config setting overlap_enabled = true still turns the feature on and emits a permanent-alias notice
REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED=1 still turns the feature on when the canonical var is unset
When legacy and canonical are both set — in TOML or in the environment — the canonical value wins
Both alias rows exist in rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY with permanent=True and remove_in is None, and their message says "permanent alias" rather than "scheduled for removal"

The two in-source readers (src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py:233, src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:765) and this repo's own rebar.toml:39 use the new name, and the only surviving occurrences of the old name are the four back-compat sites

docs/config.md documents the setting: what it produces, its three stages, that it is advisory and NEVER blocks, that its cost scales with tracker size, and that the algorithm tunables are the [tool.rebar.llm] overlap_* keys
The new permanent env rename REBAR_VERIFY_OVERLAP_ENABLED → REBAR_VERIFY_SUGGEST_DUPLICATE_TICKETS is listed in the Back-compat section of docs/config.md alongside the six existing permanent renames
No config surface is orphaned by the rename: tests/golden/config_surface.json carries both the old and new key and both env names, and the old ones are accounted for as aliases
make lint and make typecheck pass, and no file in src/rebar exceeds the module-size cap; verified by the CI module-size gate
